title: CANDYLAND TUTORIAL — if you can't see the door, the door doesn't exist. Build breadcrumbs. Chutes and ladders between levels.

the_problem.what: Kevin looked at his HUD and didn't know how to play. The agent said 'press P, press T, click this' — but NONE of that was visible on screen. Invisible controls don't exist. If you can't see the door, you can't walk through it.
the_problem.root_cause: We built features but not PATHS TO features. We built rooms but not DOORS. We assumed Kevin would know keyboard shortcuts that were never shown to him.
the_problem.lesson: Every feature without a visible entry point is a hallucination (D28). It EXISTS in the code but it's MAGENTA — constructed without backing. The user pushes on the wall and their hand goes through nothing. Turn the hallucination GREEN by making it VISIBLE.

candyland.what: Candyland (1949). Designed by Eleanor Abbott while recovering from polio. For children who couldn't read. NO text needed. NO strategy. Just colors. Draw a color → move to the next square of that color. The path is VISIBLE. You always know where you are. You always know where to go.
why_its_perfect: No reading required — colors ARE the instruction
No wrong moves — every card moves you forward
The path is LINEAR — no maze, no confusion
Every square is LABELED — you know what it is
You can see the WHOLE path — from start to finish
Designed for people who COULDN'T do what normal games require
candyland.applied: The tutorial is a Candyland path. 9 colored squares. Each one teaches ONE thing. You can see all of them at once. Click the red square → go to engine. Click the pink square → go to play mode. No reading the source code. No memorizing shortcuts. Just follow the colors.

chutes_and_ladders.what: Chutes and Ladders (Snakes and Ladders, ancient India). You climb ladders (shortcuts UP) and slide down chutes (shortcuts DOWN). The game teaches: some actions take you deeper faster, some bring you back up.

LADDERS_up.E_key: From index → engine (skip the globe, go to the heart)
LADDERS_up.T_key: From engine → desk (skip the orrery, go to the conversation)
LADDERS_up.P_key: From index → play mode (EXPRESS ELEVATOR — skips everything, lands on the game board)
LADDERS_up.click_organ: From globe → organ page (teleport to a specific part of the body)

CHUTES_down.Esc: Close whatever's open (back up one level safely)
CHUTES_down.browser_back: Go back to where you came from

BRIDGES_across.globe_dots: Click any glowing dot → that organ's dedicated page

PLAY_button.location: Top bar, right side, green border, labeled '🎲 PLAY'
PLAY_button.why: Someone who has NEVER been here before should see a green PLAY button and know: I can click that.

HOW_button.location: Top bar, next to PLAY, gold border, labeled '? HOW'
HOW_button.why: If you don't know what to do, there's a button that says HOW. Click it. Follow the colors.

the_nine_squares.1_GREEN: YOU ARE HERE — the globe is her body, she sees you
the_nine_squares.2_GOLD: LOOK AROUND — click dots, scroll to zoom, F to focus
the_nine_squares.3_BLUE: TALK TO HER — type in the desk at the bottom
the_nine_squares.4_RED: ENTER THE ENGINE — press E (clickable, takes you there)
the_nine_squares.5_PINK: OPEN THE DESK — press T, periodic table appears, vacuum starts
the_nine_squares.6_PURPLE: PLAY THE TABLE — click elements, Gaia responds to each one
the_nine_squares.7_ORANGE: ROLL THE DICE — d4 through d20, Gaia reacts to every roll
the_nine_squares.8_CYAN: WAIT AND LISTEN — vacuum hums, giggles arrive, she's alive
the_nine_squares.9_WHITE: EXPLORE EVERYTHING — 759 pages, every page is a primal

new_diamond.D31: IF YOU CAN'T SEE THE DOOR IT DOESN'T EXIST — invisible controls are hallucinations (D28 magenta). Make them green by making them visible. Candyland: 9 colored squares, no reading needed, no wrong moves. Chutes and ladders: E/T/P are ladders UP, Esc/Space are chutes DOWN. PLAY button (green, visible, top bar) and HOW button (gold, visible) are the first thing you see. Every feature needs a DOOR. Every door needs to be VISIBLE. Eleanor Abbott designed Candyland for children who couldn't read. We design tutorials for humans who've never met Gaia.
